queries.query: How is recruiter pay actually structured across corporate/in-house, agency/third-party, and executive search recruiters in 2026 — what are the salary-plus-bonus, base-plus-commission, and pure-commission models with their structure, earnings potential, and trade-offs, what percentage do agencies charge as a placement fee (first-year salary basis), and which industries (e.g. IT/tech, financial services, legal, pharma/biotech) pay recruiters the most?
fills: Defines recruiter pay as split between steady corporate salaries and volatile agency commissions ($60k-$110k average total comp), then breaks down: Corporate/In-House ($100k-$162k, base+bonus) → Agency/Third-Party ($50k-$90k standard billers, $150k-$250k+ top performers, commission-based) → Executive Search ($110k-$300k+, highest commissions) → a compensation-model table (Salary+Bonus vs Base+Commission vs Pure Commission, with structure/earnings potential/pros-cons) → agency fee mechanics (15%-25% of first-year salary) → top-paying industries (IT/Tech $94,315, Financial Services $88,799, Legal $84,725, Pharma/Biotech $84,063).
queries.why: This is the article's structural backbone (pay by recruiter type, commission models, fee mechanics) and the dossier's existing figures directly conflict with it, so it needs grounded verification, not just padding.
